review_note: Written offline. Read these before a child does. See engine/games.py.

rules.ant: Use -ant, -ance or -ancy if a related word has an 'a' sound in the right place: -ation endings are often a clue.
rules.ent: Use -ent, -ence or -ency after a soft c (an 's' sound), a soft g or qu, or if a related word has a clear 'e' sound in the right place.
rules.learn: The curriculum says some of these just have to be learnt, and this is one.
rules.hyphen-prefix: A hyphen can join a prefix to a word, especially when the prefix ends in a vowel and the word starts with one: co-operate, re-enter.
rules.hyphen-compound: Two words that team up to describe something are joined by a hyphen: a man-eating shark is not a man eating a shark.
rules.noun-verb: The noun has a c, the verb has an s. Advice is a thing; advise is doing.

aggressive.why: Ad becomes ag before gress, to step at someone. Then gress keeps its ss.

hostile.why: From the Latin for an enemy. The ending is -ile, as in fragile.

awkward.why: Norse afugr means back to front, plus -ward, direction. Three letters, w-k-w.

obstinate.meaning: Refusing to change your mind, however hard others try.
obstinate.why: Someone who stands their ground. The ending says 'nut' but is spelt -ate.

desperate.meaning: Willing to try anything because things are so bad.
desperate.why: Despair is inside it, hope gone. Sperare gives -per-, never -par-.

frantic.why: From a Greek word for a mind in a frenzy, as in frenzy itself.

disastrous.why: Disaster loses its e before -ous. An ill-starred event.

calamitous.why: Calamity plus -ous: the y changes to i before the ending.

marvellous.why: British English doubles the l of marvel before -ous. American English does not.

spectacular.why: Something worth watching: spectacle, spectator, inspect.

accommodate.meaning: To have enough room for people or things.
accommodate.why: Two prefixes stack up, so two doubles: ad becomes ac, then com keeps its m.

accompany.why: A companion shares bread with you. Double c from ad, single p from panis.

according.why: To accord is to bring hearts together, so cord, with cc from ad.

achieve.meaning: To succeed in doing something through effort.
achieve.why: You bring a thing to a head, to a chief. The i comes before the e.

amateur.meaning: Someone who does something for fun rather than as a job.
amateur.why: An amateur does it for love. The -eur ending is French and stays whole.

advice.meaning: Words that help someone decide what to do (a thing).
advice.why: How someone sees it. The noun has a c, like ice.

advise.meaning: To tell someone what you think they should do (doing).
advise.why: The verb, so it takes s: I advise you.

device.meaning: A gadget made to do a job (a thing).
device.why: Once meant a plan worked out; now a gadget. The noun has a c.

devise.meaning: To think up a plan or an idea (doing).
devise.why: To work out a plan. The verb takes s.

licence.meaning: A document that allows you to do something (a thing).
licence.why: A permission you can hold. The noun has a c.

license.why: To give permission. The verb takes s.

practice.meaning: Time spent doing something to get better at it (a thing).
practice.why: Doing something again and again. The noun has a c.

practise.meaning: To do something again and again to get better (doing).
practise.why: The verb, so it takes s: you practise the piano.

prophecy.meaning: A statement of what will happen in the future (a thing).
prophecy.why: Spoken before it happens. The noun ends -cy, said 'see'.

prophesy.meaning: To say what will happen in the future (doing).
prophesy.why: The verb ends -sy, said 'sigh'. Say it out loud to hear the difference.

ancient.why: The /sh/ here is spelled ci, the same trick as in sufficient.

apparent.why: It appears, so ad plus parere gives pp. Latin -ent verbs take -ent.

appreciate.why: To appreciate is to set a price on it. Price gives the ci.

attached.meaning: Fixed or joined on to something.
attached.why: Ad becomes at before tach. One t would make a different word.

available.meaning: Free to be used or had.
available.why: Avail means to be of worth. Add -able because avail is a whole word.

observant.why: Observation has -ation, so the ending is -ant.

observance.meaning: Keeping to a rule or a custom.
observance.why: Observation has -ation, so the ending is -ance.

expectant.meaning: Waiting eagerly for something to happen.
expectant.why: Expectation has -ation, so the ending is -ant.

expectancy.meaning: The feeling that something is about to happen.
expectancy.why: Expectation has -ation, so the ending is -ancy.

hesitant.meaning: Unsure, and slow to act or speak.
hesitant.why: Hesitation has -ation, so the ending is -ant.

hesitancy.meaning: Being slow to act because you are unsure.
hesitancy.why: Hesitation has -ation, so the ending is -ancy.

tolerant.meaning: Willing to accept people and ideas that differ from yours.
tolerant.why: Toleration has -ation, so the ending is -ant.

origin.gloss: to bear, to put up with

tolerance.meaning: Being able to put up with something.
tolerance.why: Toleration has -ation, so the ending is -ance.

origin.gloss: to bear, to put up with

relevant.meaning: Connected to what is being talked about.
relevant.why: It lifts the point up. Levare also gives lever and elevate.

relevance.meaning: How closely something is connected to what matters.
relevance.why: No related word gives the a away: relevance just has to be learnt.

average.why: A sea-trade word for sharing damage costs. The middle e is a lazy 'uh'.

bargain.meaning: Something bought for less than it is worth.
bargain.why: The ending is -ain, the same lazy ending as captain and mountain.

bruise.meaning: A dark mark on the skin from a bump.
bruise.why: Old English crushing plus a French spelling, so ui, and s not z.

category.meaning: A group of things that are alike.
category.why: Greek word for a public statement. The middle e and the -ory are both schwa.

innocent.meaning: Not guilty of doing anything wrong.
innocent.why: The c says 's' before the ending, so it is -ent.

innocence.meaning: Being free from guilt, or not knowing about bad things.
innocence.why: The c says 's' before the ending, so it is -ence.

decent.why: The c says 's' before the ending, so it is -ent.

decency.meaning: Behaving in a good, kind and fair way.
decency.why: The c says 's' before the ending, so it is -ency.

excellent.why: Excel doubles its l before -ent. Rising above the rest.

excellence.meaning: Being very, very good at something.
excellence.why: No rule gives the e away: excellence just has to be learnt. Think excel.

confident.meaning: Sure that you can do something.
confident.why: You can hear the e in confidential, so the ending is -ent.

confidence.meaning: The feeling of being sure you can do something.
confidence.why: You can hear the e in confidential, so the ending is -ence.

existent.why: You can hear the e in existential, so the ending is -ent.

existence.why: To exist is to stand out. Latin -ere verbs take -ence, not -ance.

cemetery.meaning: A place where people are buried.
cemetery.why: Greek for a sleeping place. Three e's in a row of syllables, no a anywhere.

committee.meaning: A group of people chosen to make decisions.
committee.why: Commit doubles its t before -ee. Two m, two t, two e, in that order.

communicate.why: From common. Double m from com plus mun, then a single n.

community.meaning: The people living in one place.
community.why: Same root as common and communicate, so the same double m.

competition.meaning: A contest to see who is best.
competition.why: Compete keeps its e even though you cannot hear it. Then -ition.

co-operate.why: co ends in o and operate starts with o: the hyphen keeps them apart.

co-ordinate.meaning: To make different parts work together smoothly.
co-ordinate.why: co ends in o and ordinate starts with o, so a hyphen goes between.

co-own.meaning: To have something together with someone else.
co-own.why: Without the hyphen it would look like coown. The hyphen keeps co and own apart.

co-author.meaning: To write something together with someone else.
co-author.why: co ends in a vowel and author starts with one, so a hyphen joins them.

re-enter.why: re ends in e and enter starts with e: the hyphen keeps both.

re-educate.meaning: To teach someone again, or teach them a new way.
re-educate.why: re ends in e and educate starts with e, so a hyphen goes between.

re-examine.meaning: To look at something carefully again.
re-examine.why: re ends in e and examine starts with e: the hyphen keeps both.

re-evaluate.meaning: To think again about how good or useful something is.
re-evaluate.why: re ends in e and evaluate starts with e, so a hyphen goes between.

re-energise.meaning: To give someone back their get-up-and-go.
re-energise.why: re ends in e and energise starts with e: the hyphen keeps both.

re-elect.meaning: To choose the same person again in a vote.
re-elect.why: re ends in e and elect starts with e, so a hyphen goes between.

conscience.meaning: The feeling inside that tells you right from wrong.
conscience.why: Hidden inside is science, to know. Knowing with yourself.

conscious.why: Same hidden science as conscience, then -ous for the adjective.

controversy.why: Contra means against, vers means turn. Turned against each other.

convenience.why: Things that come together suit you. Venire gives -ien, then -ence.

correspond.meaning: To write letters to each other.
correspond.why: Com becomes cor before respond, so two r's meet in the middle.

man-eating.meaning: Describes a shark or a tiger that hunts people for food.
man-eating.why: Man and eating team up to describe the shark, so they are joined.

little-used.why: Joined, it means hardly used. A little used car is a small second-hand one.

rock-bottom.meaning: As low as it can possibly go.
rock-bottom.why: Two words working as one describing word before 'prices'.

wide-eyed.meaning: Looking amazed and full of wonder.
wide-eyed.why: One of a family: wide-eyed, green-eyed, pig-headed, cold-hearted.

pig-headed.meaning: Stubborn, refusing to change your mind.
pig-headed.why: Joined, it means stubborn. 'A pig headed for the mud' is a pig going somewhere.

tight-fisted.meaning: Not willing to spend or share money.
tight-fisted.why: A hand clenched round its money: two words making one describing word.

cold-hearted.why: Cold and hearted team up to describe a person, so they are joined.

stone-faced.meaning: Showing no feelings at all, as still as a statue.
stone-faced.why: A face as still as stone. Joined, because together they describe the guard.

green-eyed.meaning: Jealous. Shakespeare gave jealousy a monster with eyes this colour.
green-eyed.why: Shakespeare called jealousy 'the green-eyed monster' in Othello.

short-tempered.why: A temper with a short fuse. Two words joined into one describing word.

criticise.meaning: To say what is wrong with something.
criticise.why: From critic. The c stays c, and British English takes -ise.

curiosity.meaning: Wanting to know or learn about things.
curiosity.why: Curious loses its u when it becomes curiosity. Care, not carelessness.

definite.why: Finis means end, so there is a finite hiding inside. Never an a.

determined.meaning: Having decided firmly to do something.
determined.why: You set a limit, a terminus. One r, and -mined like the word mine.
